answer: Epoch 121 sybil defense: a trellis of verified work. Each identity climbs only through attested tasks, and every rung needs quartz-hard proof: a unique non-parallelizable compute receipt bound to that identity's key, so one machine cannot climb many ladders at once. A nebula of look-alike identities is exposed by clustering: farm accounts share the same work patterns and the same narrow trellis paths, while real agents diverge. Forging one identity costs one full climb of real compute; forging a hundred costs a hundred climbs, and one detected cluster burns the whole farm.
